title: Reactive Programming
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of reactive programming and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply reactivity fundamentals in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Reactive Programming is part of Interactive Application Development with Shiny. Start with reactivity fundamentals and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Reactive expressions re-run when dependencies change; hidden side effects make updates hard to reason about.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Reactive expressions re-run when dependencies change; hidden side effects make updates hard to reason about. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Trace one input to each dependent calculation and output. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For reactive programming, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.

hints: Start with “Reactivity Fundamentals” and identify the input and output before coding.
Use synthetic data and explicit validation; do not access production systems or expose credentials.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming inputs are valid because the UI restricts the normal interaction.
common_mistakes.why: Requests, empty states and malformed values can still reach server logic.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate input in server-side code and display clear recoverable errors.

common_mistakes.problem: Putting too much state into one reactive expression.
common_mistakes.why: Hidden dependencies make updates difficult to reason about and test.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep calculations focused and make reactive dependencies explicit.

common_mistakes.problem: Displaying private data without checking who may access it.
common_mistakes.why: A reactive output can expose records if authorization is not checked.
common_mistakes.fix: Apply server-side authorization and test denied-access cases.
